I am an old woman, 78 years, and this small piece of land of mine is just a little plot where I grow my food mixed together — some cassava, maybe some cowpea, whatever the rains bring. I have no schooling and no money to waste on bags of fertilizer from the shop; my neighbors here in Mtwara also do not buy such things for a small plot like this. I will put the goat droppings and kitchen ash I gather, use the seed I saved from last harvest, and weed with my own hands when my grandchildren come to help. The rains will water it as they always do — I cannot carry water to this plot at my age.
